input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get the best possible speed?
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—let me know if you need anything else.
Yes, it’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002. That’s the one with the slow or unreliable data.
I tried to run a speed test, but it didn’t work—it says there’s no connection. What should I do now?
I see an airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean Airplane Mode is on? I don’t see any signal bars or network indicators like “4G” or “5G.” What should I do next?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, but it says “2G” and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see anything like “4G” or “5G.” What should I do next?

I’ve turned mobile data on and set my phone to prefer 4G and 5G networks. Now I see “5G” at the top with excellent signal bars, and it says data is enabled. Is there anything else I should do, or should I try the speed test again?
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “no connection.” I’m not sure why it’s not working, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal now. What should I do next?

I checked, and my SIM card is active and working. The APN name says “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means—does it look right to you? What should I do next?

I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. You mentioned I’ll need to reboot my phone for the changes to take effect. I’m a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get the best possible speed?

I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issues and work towards getting you the best possible speed. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format)
- Your customer ID (if you have it)

Once I have this information, I can check your line and data usage details to assist you further.
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—let me know if you need anything else.

To proceed, I’ll need you to run a quick speed test on your phone. This will help us determine your current data speed and identify any issues. Could you please run a speed test on your device and let me know the result? If you need instructions on how to do this, let me know!
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to run a speed test, but it didn’t work—it says there’s no connection. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test reports “no connection,” let’s troubleshoot your mobile data connectivity step by step.

First, I’d like to check if your phone is showing any signal or if there are any obvious issues like Airplane Mode being enabled. Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:

- Do you see any signal bars?
- Is there an airplane icon showing?
- Do you see any “4G,” “5G,” or similar network indicators?

If you’re not sure, I can guide you through checking these details on your device. Would you like step-by-step instructions?
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
I see an airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean Airplane Mode is on? I don’t see any signal bars or network indicators like “4G” or “5G.” What should I do next?

Yes, the airplane icon means Airplane Mode is currently ON. When Airplane Mode is enabled, all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off, which explains why you have no signal bars or network indicators.

To restore your mobile data and signal, please turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:

1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

Once you’ve turned it off, wait a few seconds to see if your signal bars and network indicators (like “4G” or “5G”) reappear. Let me know when you’ve done this and if your connection returns, or if you need further assistance!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, but it says “2G” and something about data being disabled. I still don’t see anything like “4G” or “5G.” What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you now see signal bars but only “2G” and a message about data being disabled, let’s address both issues:

1. Enable mobile data on your phone.
2. Change your network mode preference to allow faster networks like 4G or 5G.

Would you like step-by-step instructions for enabling mobile data and changing your network mode, or do you know how to do these on your device? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned mobile data on and set my phone to prefer 4G and 5G networks. Now I see “5G” at the top with excellent signal bars, and it says data is enabled. Is there anything else I should do, or should I try the speed test again?

That’s great progress! Now that you see “5G” with excellent signal bars and data enabled, please try running the speed test again on your device.

Let me know the result of the speed test—this will help confirm that your mobile data is working at the best possible speed. If you encounter any issues or the speed is still not excellent, please share the details, and I’ll assist you further.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “no connection.” I’m not sure why it’s not working, even though it shows 5G and excellent signal now. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone now shows “5G” and excellent signal but the speed test still reports “no connection,” let’s check a few more technical settings that could affect your mobile data:

1. APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.
2. SIM card status, to ensure your SIM is active and recognized.

Would you like step-by-step instructions to check your APN settings and SIM card status, or do you know how to check these on your device? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
Your SIM card is active and working.

I checked, and my SIM card is active and working. The APN name says “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means—does it look right to you? What should I do next?

Thank you for checking those details. Since your SIM card is active and the APN name is set to “internet,” but you’re still unable to use mobile data, it’s possible that the APN settings may not be fully correct, even if they look close.

The next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. This often resolves hidden configuration issues that can block mobile data, even when everything else looks right.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you know how to do this on your device? After resetting, you’ll also need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings as you suggested. You mentioned I’ll need to reboot my phone for the changes to take effect. I’m a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or important data by simply rebooting (restarting) your phone. Restarting your device only refreshes its system and connections—it does not delete or change any of your personal files or apps.

Please go ahead and reboot your phone now. Once it turns back on, check if your mobile data is working and try running the speed test again. Let me know the results or if you need any further help!

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? What else can we try?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since your phone shows “5G” and excellent signal, your SIM is active, APN settings have been reset, and you’ve rebooted, but you still have no data connection, this suggests a deeper technical issue that cannot be resolved with standard troubleshooting.

At this point, I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate your account and line in more detail and provide further assistance.
